title: Ctrl-F-Resist. Practices, Challenges, and Technical Needs of Civil Society Organizations Monitoring the Far-Right Online
abstract: arXiv:2609.00808v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As far-right actors increasingly exploit online platforms to disseminate ideology and mobilize supporters, civil society organizations (CSOs) play a vital yet underrecognized role in monitoring antidemocratic dynamics online. Unlike fact-checkers or content moderators, CSOs engage in long-term, contextualized analysis, often in resource-constrained settings and under precarious conditions. Despite their critical societal role, CSOs face significant barriers to adopting or co-developing technical solutions, including legal uncertainty, limited platform access, and chronic underfunding. Existing research and tool development efforts have largely overlooked these actors in favor of more institutionally embedded stakeholders. This paper addresses this gap through a qualitative study with 15 practitioners from 12 Germany-based CSOs engaged in online monitoring, positioning them as key yet overlooked stakeholders in the governance of digital

translated_title: Ctrl-F-Resist：监测极右翼线上活动的公民社会组织的实践、挑战与技术需求
translated_abstract: 随着极右翼行为者日益利用在线平台传播意识形态并动员支持者，公民社会组织（CSOs）在监测网络上的反民主动态方面发挥着至关重要却未被充分认可的作用。与事实核查员或内容审核员不同，公民社会组织从事长期的、结合具体情境的分析工作，且往往在资源受限和条件不稳定的环境下开展。尽管具有重要的社会作用，公民社会组织在采用或共同开发技术解决方案方面面临重大障碍，包括法律上的不确定性、平台访问权限受限以及长期的资金不足。然而，现有研究和工具开发工作在很大程度上忽视了这些行为者，而更倾向于关注具有制度化背景的利益相关者。本文通过对来自12家德国公民社会组织的15名从事在线监测工作的从业者进行定性研究来填补这一空白，将这些组织定位为数字治理中关键却被忽视的利益相关者。
tldr: 本文通过对12家德国公民社会组织的15名从业者进行定性研究，揭示了这些组织在极右翼在线监测工作中的长期实践、面临的挑战（法律不确定性、平台访问受限、资金不足）以及技术需求，强调它们是数字治理中被忽视的关键利益相关者。
en_tdlr: Through a qualitative study with 15 practitioners from 12 Germany-based civil society organizations, this paper examines their long-term practices, challenges, and technical needs in monitoring far-right activities online, positioning these resource-constrained organizations as key yet overlooked stakeholders in digital governance.
